arc: hook (Introducing / One assistant for every project collapsing into a star) → reveal (Made to listen) → concept (your craft / your crew / how you create) → feature (the workspace, a typed prompt, a click) → integrations (a ring of app tiles) → workflow (Nova maps out a spring launch and asks a question) → concept (building a team of helpers) → benefit (works in the cloud, nonstop) → benefit (work moves while you rest) → feature (wherever you work: phone, browser, laptop, terminal, docs) → feature (pick the model that suits the job) → benefit (your work stays private, a wall of safeguards) → recap (everything you do, linked; every task, lighter) → logo (the Nova lockup and address)

scenes.title: Headline whips off frame over a colour band, then the line collapses into one glowing star
scenes.summary: On near-black, "Introducing" enters huge from the right, shrinking and blurring as it travels, and whips off the left edge while a warm colour band runs right to left along the bottom. "One assistant" and "for every project" blur in word by word over a lattice of glowing dots that wipes in as a ground plane. The words drift apart, peak at 1.2x, then shrink uniformly into a single bright star. The star rises, the camera tilts down onto the dot floor, and the star drops toward the lens so the next scene can open inside it.
scenes.build: A camera-locked pixel stage (components/stage.ts screenLayer, 1 unit = 1 px of a 1080-tall frame) so every position reads straight off a design. Type is canvas-texture labels drawn once in white and tinted in a shader (components/type.ts label/setLabel/haloOf) whose fragment shader does a 40-tap Poisson blur with a mip bias, an optional horizontal-only smear, and a left-to-right colour sweep. The floor is an instanced point lattice (components/dotgrid.ts dotGrid + pointScale) sized in composition pixels by distance. The star is a core-plus-halo additive quad (components/fx.ts glowDot) over a shader backdrop with up to eight elliptical glows. Motion is per-frame: monotone cubic track() tables for the hand keys, sampled curves from components/ref-curves.ts for the measured ones.
scenes.reuse: Borrow for a cold open that has to feel expensive: a word travelling through the frame with motion blur, a line assembling over a ground plane, then everything converging into one point that the next scene opens out of. Swap the two lines (components/brand.ts COPY) and the accent. The curves in ref-curves.ts were measured frame by frame off a reference film, so re-time with plain interpolate() or your own track() keys rather than copying those numbers. The blurred-label shader and the dot floor are the reusable parts.

scenes.title: Star blooms into a star lattice with neon streaks drawing to their nodes, then a push through the type
scenes.summary: The scene opens inside the star left by scene 1. It blooms, the line settles back in around it, and a lattice of smaller stars arranges itself in the field. Four neon streaks draw on from off frame and land on their nodes, trailing bright heads. A slow push becomes a fast push straight through the type and out into white, which the next scene hard-cuts from.
scenes.build: Layout is stored at a reference zoom (Z_REF) and scaled per frame from a measured zoom curve, so a single camera number drives the whole field. Streaks are ribbon meshes built from a polyline with a colour ramp along their length and a draw-on parameter (components/fx.ts streak), each with a glowDot head riding the front. The handoff to white is the backdrop glow amount ramping to 1 while the layer scale runs away, so the cut lands on a flat frame.
scenes.reuse: Use as a bridge between two beats that both need to feel like one continuous move: open inside the previous scene's brightest object, settle, then push through to a flat frame the next scene can cut from. The streak ribbon and the push-to-white handoff are the transferable pieces; the star field is decoration you can replace with your own motif.

scenes.title: Hard-cut title card that lands from far away with an accent sweep across the last word
scenes.summary: A hard cut out of white. "Made to listen" arrives from far away, scaling 0.3 to 1 in about eight frames, and the blue accent sweeps across "listen" left to right in twelve frames while a blue-lavender light rises from the bottom edge of the pale ground.
scenes.build: The whole card is two shader-tinted labels over a backdrop whose glow can go negative, darkening a light ground toward a target colour instead of lighting it. The accent is the label shader's uSweep uniform moving across the plane's uv.x with a soft edge, so one word changes colour mid-letter without a second mesh. Scale and the sweep position are sampled curves from ref-curves.ts.
scenes.reuse: A 1.4 second title card worth lifting whole: the land-from-distance entrance plus a colour sweep that inks one word is a cheap way to make a short line feel deliberate. Swap the two words and the accent colour. Works on light or dark ground because the glow is signed.

scenes.title: Three-line list rolling upward like a picker wheel, each line lit as it crosses the window
scenes.summary: "your craft", "your crew", "how you create" scroll upward on a pale ground. Each takes its turn at full white while the lines above and below sit back, soft and translucent, like the window of a date picker.
scenes.build: One continuous measured scroll offset drives all three labels at a fixed pitch. Brightness and blur are functions of a line's distance from the lit band, not of a per-line schedule, so the list stays coherent at any speed and adding a fourth item needs no new timing. The scroll eases quickly through each handoff and drifts slowly while a line is lit.
scenes.reuse: The cheapest way to say three things in three seconds. Swap COPY.list in components/brand.ts and the pitch constant; anything from two to six items works because the lighting is positional. Good for a values list, a feature list or an audience list.

scenes.title: Pull back from a window corner to the whole app, push into the composer, type a prompt and click send
scenes.summary: A close-up of a rounded window corner pulls back to the whole product window: top bar with the mark and name, a left rail of icons and unreadable bars, and the greeting "Good evening, Sam / What should we tackle today?". The camera pushes into the composer, a file chip drops in and "Draft a plan for our spring launch" types itself, then the shot rushes to the send button, a cursor glides in from the lower right and clicks, and blue light pushes out from the pressed button until it floods the frame.
scenes.build: The whole interface is one canvas-drawn plane (components/ui.ts canvasPlane, rr, text, bars, drawMark) rendered once at 2x, so there is no DOM and nothing to lay out per frame. The camera is three sampled tracks (zoom, x, y) on the stage layer, which means a single timeline retimes the entire shot. The typed prompt is one pre-drawn plane per prefix length, swapped by frame, so typing costs nothing at render time. The flood is a radial shader quad (components/fx.ts flood) expanding from the button's screen position.
scenes.reuse: The default way to show software in this template. Borrow the pattern: draw your UI once into a canvas plane, then move the camera rather than the content, and end on a flood that hands off to the next scene. Replace the window drawing, the greeting, the prompt string (PROMPT) and the chip label. The pre-rendered-prefix trick is worth keeping for any typing animation.

scenes.title: Word assembles from scattered letters, then a ring of eighteen app tiles orbits and swells past the frame
scenes.summary: Out of the blue flood, "Plugged in" assembles from letters scattered across the frame. The word shrinks away as eighteen rounded app tiles fly in and form a ring that orbits three supporting lines, "to your apps", "your files", "every corner of your day". The ring then swells outward past the frame edges to hand off to the next scene.
scenes.build: Each letter is its own shader label, positioned from measured glyph widths so the assembled word has correct spacing without a layout engine. The tiles are canvas-drawn rounded squares (components/ui.ts tile) placed on a circle whose radius and spin are sampled tracks, so the orbit speeds up and the ring blows past the camera on the same two numbers.
scenes.reuse: The standard integrations beat: a ring of platform tiles around a claim. Replace tile(i) with your real logos (drawn into the same canvas plane, or textures loaded through ctx.manager) and set N_TILES to how many you have. The letter-scatter assembly is independently useful for any word that should feel gathered rather than typed.

scenes.title: Agent builds a scrolling step list, the camera pulls out to the whole plan and pushes into its question
scenes.summary: The product mark streaks in big from the lower left, settles small and slides aside as "Mapping it out…" arrives. A step list builds one row at a time, "Reading Launch notes", "Pulling last spring's timeline", "Checking the team calendar", "Weighing budget and dates", "Drafting the plan", scrolling as it grows. The camera pulls out to show the whole plan document inside the app shell, then pushes into Nova's question at the bottom, "Ready when you are. Shall I line up…". A reply composer slides up, types "Go ahead!" and a cursor clicks send.
scenes.build: Two layers of fidelity on one canvas-plane stack: a readable step column drawn at full size, and the surrounding document and app shell drawn as grey bars (components/ui.ts bars) that only becomes visible when the camera pulls out. Steps appear on an explicit frame list (STEP_AT) at a fixed pitch rather than a stagger formula, so a step can be retimed without touching its neighbours. Camera zoom and offset are three sampled tracks covering the whole 12 second shot.
scenes.reuse: The best scene here for showing an agent or a long-running process actually working. Borrow the two-fidelity trick: real type for what the viewer must read, grey bars for everything the camera will never hold on. Swap the step strings, the question and the reply. Keep the pull-out-then-push-in rhythm, it is what makes a list of steps read as one thought.

scenes.title: Soft headline, then a ring of glossy toy-like shapes bursts outward around the second line
scenes.summary: The send from the previous scene lands on "Building a team" over "of helpers" in dark ink on a pale ground. On a hard cut, a ring of glossy rounded shapes bursts outward from the centre around "to finish / the hard stuff", growing past the frame as the scene ends.
scenes.build: The shape ring is seeded by a small deterministic PRNG (mulberry32) rather than Math.random, which is what keeps the burst identical on every render and in the export. Radius is a single sampled track, so the burst accelerates with one curve. Type is the same shader labels as everywhere else, swapped on a hard cut at a named frame constant.
scenes.reuse: A short connective beat for a claim that needs motion but no information. The seeded-PRNG burst is the piece to lift: any deterministic scatter in this engine needs it, because Math.random is banned. Swap the four words and recolour the shapes.

scenes.title: Night stage where orbs streak in on neon trails and drop off labelled helper pills, then a panning reveal
scenes.summary: On a dark stage, glowing orbs fly in along curved neon trails and each drops a labelled pill where it lands: Research helper, Budget helper, Launch planner, Review helper, Outreach helper, Notes helper, in blue, red, green and amber. The stage pans right as more helpers join, the curved trails straighten into horizon lines, and "Works in the cloud, nonstop" punches in one word at a time. A light streak flashes the frame to white.
scenes.build: Each helper is a path of frame-fraction control points turned into a ribbon streak (components/fx.ts streak) with a glowDot comet riding its draw-on parameter; the comet carries past its pill and fades. The pan is one sampled track applied to the stage group, so adding a seventh helper is one array entry plus a pan key. The word punches are per-word labels with their own in and out frames, and the exit resolves to pure white so the next scene's ground matches.
scenes.reuse: Use when several named things have to arrive one after another and feel like a system rather than a list: agents, regions, integrations, team members. Replace the HELPERS array (name, colour, landing position, path) and the WORDS array. The comet-on-a-ribbon pattern is the transferable piece.

scenes.title: Two-line promise writes on word by word, then a finished task lifts off the home screen
scenes.summary: Out of the white flash, "so work moves" and "while you rest" write on word by word with the last word inking blue. A hard cut puts us on the product home screen, "Hi Sam" with an activity column; the camera pushes into the task list and one completed task lifts off the page on a soft glow.
scenes.build: The two lines are per-word labels laid out from measured widths, with the final word tinted through the label shader rather than drawn separately. The home screen is a canvas plane again, and the lift is a duplicate of the task row translated on z with a glow quad beneath it, so one row appears to peel off a flat texture. Camera zoom and offset are sampled tracks across the cut.
scenes.reuse: Borrow the lift: drawing a UI flat and then peeling one element out of it on z is a cheap, convincing way to point at a single row without rebuilding the interface as geometry. Swap L1 and L2 and the task strings.

scenes.title: Travelling shot down a row of tilted screens with a label that changes as each one passes
scenes.summary: "Help that follows you, / wherever you work" on navy, then a long lateral move along a row of tilted surfaces where the product lives: phone, browser window, laptop, terminal, a grid of docs tiles, and a chat thread. A label above changes with each one, "on your phone", "in the browser", "on your laptop", "in the terminal", "in your docs", "and everywhere else". Screens near frame centre turn a touch more toward camera, and a bar of light runs along the bottom as the shot ends.
scenes.build: Every device is a canvas plane on a shared row group; one sampled x track moves the whole row, timed so each screen crosses frame centre exactly while its label is up. The per-screen turn is a y-rotation driven by distance from centre, which is what stops the row reading as flat cardboard. Labels are a data array of prefix plus keyword with explicit in and out frames, so the copy and the travel are retimed independently.
scenes.reuse: The canonical multi-surface beat, and the easiest scene here to re-skin: edit the LABELS array and the six draw functions. Works for platforms, devices, locales or product modes. Keep the rule that the travel timing and the label timing are two separate tables.

scenes.title: Promise builds word by word, then a cursor opens a model picker and the list unfolds
scenes.summary: "Pick the brain / that suits the job" builds word by word on a pale ground, the first line alone and large before both settle smaller. We drop into the composer, a cursor opens the model chip and the menu unfolds: Smart (Nova picks for you, checked), Nova Swift (Quick answers, New), Nova Deep (Long, careful work), Nova Lite (Light and fast). The camera eases out to show the whole menu while a hover highlight follows the cursor down the list.
scenes.build: The two lines are laid out from measured widths twice, at the large and the settled size, and interpolated between those two positions, so the reflow is exact rather than eyeballed. The menu is a canvas plane; the hover highlight is a separate rounded quad whose y follows the cursor track, which is why hovering costs no redraw. Camera zoom and offset are sampled tracks.
scenes.reuse: Use for any picker, plan selector or mode switch: a cursor opening a real-looking menu reads as a product doing something, where a static list does not. Swap the MODELS array and the two headline lines. The measure-at-two-sizes-and-lerp technique is worth copying for any headline that changes size mid-scene.

scenes.title: Three glowing rings stretch into the first pill of a wall of safeguards that cascades in row by row
scenes.summary: On near-black, "Your work stays private" with the last word inking blue, then "with controls your / security team trusts". Three glowing rings drift together and stretch into the first outlined pill, and a wall of nine safeguards cascades in row by row: Never trains on your data, Role-based access, Encrypted end to end, Audit trail for every action, Asks before big moves, Data stays in your region, Policy checks on every helper, Private by default, Spend limits you set, each pill outlined and shadowed in its own colour.
scenes.build: Each pill is a canvas plane sized from the measured width of its label plus fixed padding, drawn with a coloured shadowBlur behind a near-black fill and a 2px stroke in the same colour, so the neon outline needs no shader. Rows are a nested array, which makes the cascade a double index rather than a hand-written stagger. The rings-into-pill move is a scale on x only, from a circle to the pill's aspect.
scenes.reuse: The compliance and trust beat, and a clean pattern for any 'wall of claims' ending: five to twelve short strings in rows, cascading. Replace ROWS with your own and keep the colours few. The measured-width pill is reusable anywhere you need a chip that fits its text exactly.

scenes.title: Spiralling dot vortex carries two lines with a scrambling last word, then a dive and an orb circling the close
scenes.summary: A spiralling vortex of dots carries "Everything you do, linked" and then "Every task, lighter"; each line's last word scrambles through random glyphs for eight frames before settling with a colour glow, and the first line rises to make room for the second. The camera dives into the vortex, and on deep blue an orb streaks in on a trail, circles the closing promise, then rushes the lens and floods the frame toward the white end card.
scenes.build: The glyph scramble picks from a fixed character table indexed by frame, not by a random call, so it is identical on every render. The vortex is instanced glow quads on a spiral whose angle and radius are functions of frame and index. After the dive, the orb follows three sampled tracks (x, y, scale) rather than a parametric curve, which is what lets it loiter and then accelerate. The close is a radial flood quad (components/fx.ts flood).
scenes.reuse: A finale shape worth copying wholesale: recap lines inside a moving field, a dive, then one object that circles the last promise and rushes the lens into the end card. Swap the LINES array (each entry is a lead-in, a punch word and its frame range). The deterministic scramble is reusable for any text that should look like it is resolving.

scenes.title: Mark resolves out of a white flood, slides left as the wordmark arrives, and the address settles under the lockup
scenes.summary: On white, the product mark scales in at centre with a slight counter-rotation, then slides left into its place in the lockup as the wordmark "Nova" blurs in from the right. The address "nova.example/work" settles underneath, and the whole lockup breathes gently while it holds for about three seconds.
scenes.build: The lockup is laid out from the measured width of the wordmark, so the mark, the gap and the word stay optically centred whatever the name is; change the word and nothing needs re-centring by hand. The mark itself is drawn into a canvas plane (components/ui.ts drawMark/markPlane) as a gradient disc with an offset bright core and a small orbiting dot. The hold is a sine breath on scale plus a slow upward ramp, which keeps the last seconds from reading as a freeze frame.
scenes.reuse: Drop-in end card for any brand. Replace drawMark with your logo (or a texture loaded through ctx.manager), set the wordmark string and the address. Keep the measured-width lockup and the breathing hold.
